content.text: {"questions": [{"type": "mcq", "question": "A bar is cut into 2 equal parts, 1 part shaded. Another same-size bar is cut into 4 equal parts. How many parts should be shaded to show the same amount?", "options": ["1 part", "2 parts", "3 parts", "4 parts"], "answer": "2 parts", "explanation": "1/2 is equivalent to 2/4, so 2 out of 4 parts must be shaded.", "tag": "skill_based"}, {"type": "mcq", "question": "Which fraction is equivalent to 1/3?", "options": ["2/3", "2/6", "1/6", "3/3"], "answer": "2/6", "explanation": "Multiply both numerator and denominator by 2: 1/3 = 2/6.", "tag": "understanding"}, {"type": "mcq", "question": "Two bars are the same length. Bar A has 3 out of 6 parts shaded. Bar B has 1 out of 2 parts shaded. What can you say?", "options": ["Bar A shows more", "Bar B shows more", "Both show the same amount", "Cannot compare"], "answer": "Both show the same amount", "explanation": "3/6 and 1/2 shade the same area, so they are equivalent fractions.", "tag": "logical_reasoning"}, {"type": "mcq", "question": "Which is greater, 1/3 or 1/5?", "options": ["1/3", "1/5", "Both are equal", "Cannot say"], "answer": "1/3", "explanation": "When the numerator is the same, fewer, bigger parts mean a greater fraction, so 1/3 is greater.", "tag": "understanding"}, {"type": "short", "question": "Draw two bars of the same length. Shade one to show 2/4 and the other to show 1/2. What do you notice about the shaded parts?", "answer": "Both shaded parts cover the same amount, showing 2/4 and 1/2 are equivalent.", "explanation": "Equal shaded area in same-size bars means the fractions are equivalent.", "tag": "skill_based"}, {"type": "short", "question": "Find a fraction equivalent to 2/5 with denominator 10.", "answer": "4/10", "explanation": "Multiply both numerator and denominator by 2: 2/5 = 4/10.", "tag": "application"}, {"type": "short", "question": "A child says 1/2 is equivalent to 2/2 because they just doubled the top number. Explain what mistake the child made.", "answer": "The child changed only the numerator and forgot to change the denominator too; both must be multiplied by the same number.", "explanation": "To make an equivalent fraction, multiply numerator and denominator by the same number.", "tag": "logical_reasoning"}, {"type": "short", "question": "Order these fractions from smallest to greatest using bar models: 1/2, 1/8, 1/4.", "answer": "1/8, 1/4, 1/2", "explanation": "With the same numerator, a bigger denominator means smaller pieces, so 1/8 is smallest and 1/2 is largest.", "tag": "application"}, {"type": "mcq", "question": "Which statement is correct about 3/4 and 3/10?", "options": ["3/10 is greater because 10 is bigger than 4", "3/4 is greater because the parts are bigger", "They are equal", "Cannot compare them"], "answer": "3/4 is greater because the parts are bigger", "explanation": "With the same numerator, fewer and bigger parts (denominator 4) give a greater fraction than more, smaller parts (denominator 10).", "tag": "logical_reasoning"}, {"type": "short", "question": "Two bars of different lengths both show 1 part shaded out of 2 equal parts. Can we say both represent the same fraction amount? Why or why not?", "answer": "The fraction 1/2 is the same in both, but the actual shaded amount is different because the bars are different sizes; we must compare fractions using same-size wholes.", "explanation": "Fractions only show equal amounts when the wholes are the same size.", "tag": "understanding"}]}
